title: Seeing Multilingual Learners through Media and AI: Pre-Service Teachers’ Perceptions in an ESOL Course
venue: Journal of Interdisciplinary Research in Artificial Intelligence and Society
extended_summary:
This paper examines how pre-service teachers in an ESOL Foundations course understood the influence of media and generative AI on perceptions of multilingual learners, and how they translated those understandings into possible classroom practices. The authors frame the problem as a teacher-preparation challenge: future K–12 teachers increasingly encounter algorithmically curated media and AI-generated content that may shape deficit-oriented beliefs about immigrant and multilingual communities, yet preparation programs often emphasize technical digital skills more than critical evaluation.

The study used an exploratory instrumental case study design centered on one upper-level undergraduate ESOL course at a university in Southwest Florida during Spring 2024. The course included a teacher-attitudes module with assigned readings and a structured class discussion/activity focused on media representation, credibility, and AI-enabled misinformation. Data came from two coursework artifacts: a reading reflection paper and written responses to the class discussion/activity. Thirty-eight undergraduate pre-service teachers participated, mostly women, and the cohort included both monolingual English speakers and bilingual students.

Analysis of the written artifacts produced five themes: media as a curriculum for bias, uncertainty about authenticity and AI-generated content, a perceived gap between computer use and critical media reasoning, movement from diagnosis to classroom design, and links between media/AI literacy and equity-oriented teaching commitments. Overall, participants saw media literacy and foundational AI literacy as important for challenging biased narratives and for supporting more equitable instruction for multilingual learners. The authors argue that critical media literacy and AI literacy should be treated as core professional competencies in teacher education, especially in courses preparing teachers for multilingual classrooms.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generic generative AI systems that can produce or manipulate text, images, or audio content.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper discussed generative AI as part of the contemporary information environment shaping pre-service teachers’ perceptions of multilingual learners, and used an AI-generated image in a class activity to prompt verification and provenance reasoning.

quality_tier_rationale: This is an exploratory qualitative instrumental case study rather than an intervention or causal impact study. It provides useful descriptive evidence about perceptions and proposed practices, but does not test an AI tool’s effectiveness.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper suggests meaningful implications for teacher preparation and critical AI/media literacy, but it reports no outcome effects on student learning or teacher performance and includes no quantitative impact estimates.
